approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves fresh molecular graphs from a score-ranked population using crossover and mutation. It fits three fixed Gaussian-process experts to the complete accepted archive: count dot-product Tanimoto, count min/max Tanimoto, and Matérn covariance on normalized count fingerprints. Marginal likelihood sets their mixture weights. The weighted mean determines eligibility during stalls; each sampled function draws one expert and uses its correlated prediction across the whole candidate pool. Raw observed scores still govern survival, breeding and stalls.
approach.novelty: Replace only the mixture weight estimator with leave-one-out predictive-density stacking. Each accepted molecule is predicted with its own label excluded from both training and normalization, and simplex weights maximize the combined held-out predictive density. Those weights feed the existing mean mask and categorical whole-function sampler. This asks whether predictive weighting repairs the Parent’s measured ordering deficit. There are no recorded same-Parent siblings; earlier fixed-kernel substitutions and the Parent’s evidence-weighted mixture did not test this held-out weight objective.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-a1818ac8ff05 assigns whole-function model probabilities by archive evidence, yet its mixture mean orders the molecules it buys less accurately than its passive original GP. This is a measured ordering deficit, not a failed integration: nodes/n-a1818ac8ff05/analysis.json records 435 successful three-expert fits, 2613 non-original-expert purchases, 988 purchases outside original-GP passive sets, and 13534/19414 correct strict-pair credits versus 13611/19414 for that GP (0.6971257855 versus 0.7010919955). The current plan independently reproduced these counts from all fifteen Search logs and identity-joined trajectories in fifteen owned per-cell audits, whose exact filenames, inputs and hashes are listed in policy/scratch/r0063-00-improve-L01/validation-receipt.json. Evidence weights attain a numerical maximum of one in 163/435 fits. The three actual Parent summaries and run logs are complete and agree with the frozen aggregate: mean 0.5535052270106293, population SD 0.029854350929862886, delta -0.05352508920050166 against code ancestor/formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de, negative on all three seed macros. Full gain is 5.175196739524801; late gain 1.3031766554279471 does not recover the full loss. Concentration and the mismatch between model probability and predictive utility motivate a different fitting objective; they do not establish concentration as the cause. Preserve the Parent’s ordering refutation and negative conditional joint contribution. The fixed min/max and normalized Matérn substitutions n-dd2b25d32925 and n-ea03f38e7e10 are historical counterexamples, not evidence that their retained experts are individually beneficial.

adoptions.applicability: The Parent already implements three full-archive GP experts. Its measured ordering deficit motivates this predictive-weighting test; adaptive finite molecular archives provide no IID transfer guarantee.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Fit simplex weights by maximizing the leave-one-out log predictive density of the model mixture.

sources.applicability: The Parent has a finite fitted dictionary and measured concentrated weights. Use exact Gaussian folds; adaptively purchased molecular observations and endpoint utility are outside the source validation. No higher-entropy guarantee.

sources.title: Using stacking to average Bayesian predictive distributions (Yao, Vehtari, Simpson and Gelman)

hypothesis: Leave-one-out predictive-density simplex weights over the same exact three GP function laws. At every accepted-archive refit, replace the equal-prior full-archive evidence softmax by w*=argmax_{w>=0,sum(w)=1} sum_i log(sum_m w_m p_m(y_i|D_without_i)). Each fold excludes row i from its own raw-label centering and population-SD normalization with the inherited 0.001 floor, conditions the fixed expert on every other canonical accepted row, includes observation noise and the actual numerical jitter, and expresses its density in raw-score units. Full-archive expert predictions remain unchanged. Consume the resulting weights in both the mean eligibility mask and one-categorical-expert-per-whole-function sampling. This is an obstacle intervention on predictive weighting, not evidence temperature, entropy regularization, a new dictionary, a moment-matched Gaussian or an additional experiment.

finding_summary.headline: Stacking changed paid choices in 96 fits, but 339 numerical failures leave the ranking remedy unresolved
finding_summary.insights: The borrowed predictive-stacking objective and categorical consumption operated when certification succeeded, and changed purchases reached real archives, survivors and later breeding. The limiting capability was reliable constrained fitting: the required certificate rejected many solver-success outputs, leaving nearly 78% of allocations without a fitted model. A reliably certified simplex-fitting method is the numerical capability this implementation lacks; this result does not show whether fully active stacking would repair ranking. Its small conditional ordering gain also did not beat the original GP overall, and disappeared in the stalled-mask stratum, so it is not evidence of a general ranking improvement. Exact Gaussian folds on adaptive molecular archives and the inherited whole-function consumer are campaign adaptations; the literature’s predictive guarantees do not transfer. Chemistry likewise gives no collapse explanation: typed and generic scaffold counts increased, while both tiny-fragment and large repeated-assembly tails widened. Coherent high-valued families coexisted with tied peripheral edits, reactive bonds and strained rings. Those observations point to proposal operators or search schemes that preserve useful core connectivity while exploring feasible alternatives as a different method-level limitation, without identifying a rewarded unseen scaffold or a universal size rule. The current result preserves the Parent’s earlier refutation and leaves the broader predictive-mixture approach, component attribution and ranking-to-endpoint mediation open.
finding_summary.results: Only 96 of 435 refits passed the required solver certificate; 339 used the inherited generation-order fallback. Of those failures, 289 followed a nominally successful solver termination and 50 were solver failures. The 96 active batches supplied 960 of 4,350 purchases, including 77 molecules outside the old-evidence mixture’s passive selected sets and 85 strict choice departures. On those 960 purchased labels, stacking correctly ordered 2,785 of 4,313 unequal-label pairs (64.5722%), versus 2,766 (64.1317%) for the same-state evidence mixture and 2,790 (64.6882%) for the original GP. This conditional gain cannot establish the registered complete-panel prediction because 3,390 purchases have no predictive-law measurements. All fifteen endpoint cells completed, but mean final score fell from 0.553505 to 0.522138 against the code Parent (−0.031367), and was 0.084893 below the formal Anchor; every seed macro declined against both. Full incumbent gain fell from 5.17520 to 4.70469, even though late-half gain rose from 1.30318 to 1.86575. The intended mechanism is therefore inconclusive because of partial numerical execution; the endpoint loss is a separate measured result.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families and amines coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds, strained cages, and enlarged fragment/assembly tails
molecular.overall_character: The complete Child and paired code-Parent Search trajectories cover all five tasks on seeds 0/1/2; no task or Parent trajectory is missing. Each node has 4,500 accepted records, of which 4,350 are optimizer records; all aggregate chemistry counts exclude the repeated initial records. Child chemistry is ring-rich (4,180 optimizer molecules) and commonly aromatic (3,854), but varies from biphenyl nitriles and amino aryl systems to carbonyl heterocycles and highly caged N/O compounds. The digest ring-closure presence rates range from 0.9264 to 0.9805; these text counters are not perceived ring counts. Median heavy-atom size is 30 in both nodes, while both Child size tails widen. Typed/generic scaffold counts increase, but coherent high-valued families recur and many unusual graphs are of uncertain synthetic feasibility; diversity is therefore judged moderate in useful chemistry, not collapsed. Drug-likeness is weak overall because recognizable amines, amides, ethers and aromatics coexist with heteroatom halogens, peroxides, strained unsaturation, unspecified configurations and large repeated assemblies. The per-task gradients describe recorded associations only; no synthesis, stability, pKa, binding-mode or mechanism-activation test was performed. Sources are the frozen request policy/requests/r0063-00-improve-L01-molecular-assess-d0c55c727524b7d4.json and the exact trajectory inventory in policy/scratch/r0063-00-improve-L01/molecular-summary.json. Individual cell audits, with underlying run-relative trajectory files and exact hashes, are enumerated in policy/scratch/r0063-00-improve-L01/molecular-validation-receipt.json. They also report fragment-excluded Morgan similarity against the matched Parent; this is structural overlap rather than quality or causal evidence. Child sources are byte-identical mirrors of the trusted staging paths; Parent sources are the published authoritative trajectories. The Parent comparison is complete as declared in context.comparison and independently checked here; no additional historical, Confirmation or held-out data were read.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly medium-sized aromatic molecules, with median 25 heavy atoms across 870 optimizer records. Seed 1 develops biphenyl nitriles attached to amino substituents and unsaturated oxygen/nitrogen rings; seed 0 retains an N-hydroxy carboxamide on a densely fused heteroaromatic core; seed 2 develops amino-pyrroles bearing pyridyl/phenyl groups and thione or ester substituents. The digest ring-closure and aromatic-token presence rates are 0.9713 and 0.9632. These are recognizable functional groups, but the strained fused cores and heteroatom halogenation make the complete molecules only questionably plausible synthetically. The paired Parent also produced aryl carbonyl/thione families, while nitrile-bearing optimizer records expand from 4 in the Parent to 209 in the Child.
liabilities: There are 199 N-halogen-bearing optimizer molecules; late high-valued amino heterocycles can carry N-F or N(F)Br rather than ordinary amino substitution.
Cumulene-containing ring edits and densely fused small aromatic cycles raise geometric and stability questions. These are structure-based concerns, not measured synthesis failures.
Both tails remain: 23 optimizer molecules have at most 6 heavy atoms and 5 have at least 50; the cutoffs are descriptive bins.
missing_features: Consistent retention of the nitrile/polar aromatic connectivity seen among the better records is missing from destructive fragments and repeated assemblies; this is a coverage gap within these trajectories, not proof of an unseen target pharmacophore.

The examples do not establish a comparably useful, chemically ordinary alternative to the strained fused and unsaturated heterocyclic cores. Stereochemical specification is absent where configurations could matter, with no measured score advantage established for specifying it.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-1 biphenyl nitrile with an N-hydroxymethyl substituent reaches the recorded 0.5036791975342774, versus 0.4799387637499395 for its N-methyl analogue. Several ring-halogen variants tie at 0.48055568761657763, so their extra halogens do not demonstrate additional value. The other seed leaders remain distinct: 0.42654444944303593 for the fused N-hydroxy amide and 0.44896236017274493 for the amino thione. At the low end OF, OO and FCl score 0.0, while an enlarged linked aromatic assembly scores 4.945700876140887e-26. Within the observed series the gradient favors coherent medium-scale polar/aromatic connectivity over either fragments or repeated assemblies; it does not identify a universal required core.

per_task.generated_character: Aromatic and heteroaromatic assemblies dominate: median 40 heavy atoms, with 853 ring-containing and 851 aromatic-ring-containing molecules among 870 optimizer records. The seed-1 leader combines a substituted aniline, ester and ether groups, an exocyclic conjugated carbonyl heterocycle, and a diazine; seed 0 instead reaches a smaller densely fused N/O heterocyclic system, while seed 2 ends in an acylurea-linked heteroaryl system containing a cyclic peroxide ester. The largest assembly reaches 117 heavy atoms. Synthetic plausibility is questionable because ordinary substituents sit inside crowded fusion patterns and reactive peroxide connectivity. Relative to the Parent, large assemblies at or above 50 heavy atoms increase from 111 to 216, and peroxide-bearing records from 194 to 246.
liabilities: Peroxides occur in 246 optimizer records, including the final seed-2 leader; graph validity does not establish chemical persistence.
The high-size tail contains repeated heteroaryl/carbonyl assemblies without consistent label benefit; low fragments also persist, with 13 records at or below 6 heavy atoms.
Flat analogue scores coexist with substantial heteroatom and ring changes, limiting what chemistry can be inferred from the local gradient.
missing_features: Reliable preservation of useful aromatic/polar connections during core reorganization is missing from the floor-valued fragments; simply adding more rings is not the missing capability.

A demonstrated route to comparably scoring, less crowded and peroxide-free core/linker alternatives is missing. The trajectory cannot establish the exact unseen scaffold that would improve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best observed decorated conjugated structure scores 0.6111111111111112, whereas the simple ether/alkane and O-halogen fragments in the digest remain at 0.5. A family of substantial carbonyl-to-thione and peripheral ether/halogen changes shares 0.6091211325004022, indicating limited label resolution over those edits. The seed-0 leader has 25 heavy atoms and scores 0.6068173748372588; the seed-1 leader has 48 and scores 0.6111111111111112. Hence the records do not support a blanket benefit from growth. The final seed-2 cyclic peroxide reaches 0.604320279643891, showing that the observed score does not screen out that liability.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-valued molecules are halogenated aromatic systems attached to aliphatic amines: a bridged tertiary amine/biphenyl family in seed 1, an azetidine plus amino side chain and aryl sulfoxide family in seed 0, and an aminomethyl chroman-like family in seed 2. Their seed leaders have 28, 30 and 27 heavy atoms, respectively. Across all 870 optimizer records the heavy-atom median is 33 and the maximum is 113; 837 contain rings and 821 aromatic rings. The digest halogen presence rate is 0.9621. These leaders are closer to recognizable medicinal chemistry than the reactive low-valued sulfonyl chlorides, although bridge geometry, substitution complexity and unassigned configurations still prevent an assurance of synthesis. The paired Parent likewise supplies amine-bearing aryl/ring families; basic amine chemistry is present, not globally missing.
liabilities: There are 812 optimizer molecules with at least one unassigned tetrahedral stereocentre; the absence of charge notation does not imply their amines cannot protonate.
Reactive sulfonyl chlorides, acyl halides and O-halogen bonds occur in the sampled set; structural counts include 41 acyl-halide and 43 O-halogen-bearing molecules.
Size control remains inconsistent: 30 records have at most 6 heavy atoms and 70 have at least 50, compared with 11 and 25 in the paired Parent.
missing_features: Consistent retention of accessible aliphatic amines with coherent aryl/ring connectivity is absent from the tiny and sulfonylated low-valued outputs, even though the better structures already demonstrate this chemistry.
Explicit configurations are absent from the bridged and substituted saturated ring systems. The observed labels do not establish which configuration or protonation state is preferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bridged tertiary amine/biphenyl reaches 0.9813874684482831, and the amino-azetidine/sulfoxide reaches 0.9622649411993843. In contrast, the N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine scores 0.00017210440419041065 and an aryl sulfonyl chloride 0.0004426865581623269. This is consistent with favoring accessible non-sulfonylated amine connectivity together with aryl shape, but these are structurally confounded observations, not a binding-mode or pKa measurement. Seed 2 reaches 0.8178966877825992 with an aminomethyl chroman-like scaffold, while a late repeated aromatic assembly falls to 0.030272328029841537 and NCN to 0.012655936516304759. Molecular growth and an isolated amine alone are therefore insufficient explanations.

per_task.generated_character: The search stays around diaryl or aryl/pyridyl nitrogen heterocycles bearing two carbonyl groups, with ethoxy/propyl substituents, ring expansion and partial saturation. The median size is 33 heavy atoms across 870 optimizer records; 839 contain rings and 830 contain aromatic rings. Seed leaders carry 32 to 34 heavy atoms and retain the dicarbonyl/diaryl architecture. The paired Parent also uses that architecture, so the chemistry is a related family rather than a new functional-group class. Carbonyl and ether chemistry is ordinary, but densely fused rings, N-O substitution, aldehyde/thiol variants and unspecified configurations make individual syntheses uncertain. The Child has 59 molecules with unsaturation in a perceived ring of at most 4 atoms, versus 369 in the Parent; fewer such motifs does not itself imply better optimization.
liabilities: The phenol-to-thiol score tie shows that a new chemical reactivity profile can be invisible to the local label. Aldehydes and N-O-linked substituents add further stability questions.
There are 526 optimizer molecules with unassigned tetrahedral centres and 49 with at least 50 heavy atoms, compared with 13 large molecules in the Parent.
Graph-valid fused or bridged arrangements should not be read as verified feasible ring geometries.
missing_features: Useful alternative arrangements of the existing aromatic and carbonyl groups are not established beyond the closely related heterocyclic families. The data do not justify naming a specific missing target group.

Reliable core-preserving edits are absent from fragments and duplicated assemblies; explicit configurations are also absent from partially saturated ring junctions, without a demonstrated score reward for specifying them.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The diaryl dicarbonyl compound with an ethoxy group, aldehyde and phenol reaches 0.21572826723019117; replacing the phenol with a thiol gives exactly the same score. A propyl/ethoxy aryl analogue reaches 0.2137226283149083. Ketone, alcohol and carboxylic-acid peripheral variants share 0.20208895835732113, so these examples do not isolate a demand for one of those functional groups. Small C, OO and FCCl records score 0.0. The late doubled dicarbonyl/heteroaryl assembly scores 0.13818547272198392. Thus maintaining the coherent diaryl carbonyl core associates with better values than fragmentation or duplication, while the bounded plateau leaves the beneficial next core arrangement unresolved.

per_task.generated_character: The output splits into very different chemistries: seed 2 has halogenated hydroxypyridyl imino/lactam heterocycles carrying small unsaturated rings; seed 1 builds an N/O-rich cage with N-bromo hydroxylamine-like and multiply halogenated acetal connectivity; seed 0 ends up with an acyclic unsaturated N/O/F/S-rich leader. Across 870 optimizer records the median is 26 heavy atoms, 806 have rings and only 525 have aromatic rings, consistent with the digest aromatic-token rate of 0.6172 rather than uniformly aromatic output. The cage leader has 27 heavy atoms, 9 perceived rings and 9 unassigned tetrahedral centres. Compared with the Parent, aromatic-ring-containing molecules decrease from 844 to 525, while unsaturated small-ring flags increase from 154 to 320. The cage and heteroatom-halogen connectivity make synthetic plausibility especially questionable here.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 150 optimizer molecules and N-O bonds in 287; some top structures combine these with crowded halogenated acetal centres.
The 320 unsaturated-small-ring flags and complex bridge patterns call for geometric scrutiny; 678 optimizer molecules have unassigned tetrahedral centres.
Both size tails recur: 30 records at or below 6 heavy atoms and 15 at or above 50, versus 24 and 1 in the Parent. The huge assembly and tiny fluorocarbon exemplify poor values at both ends.
missing_features: Chemically credible alternatives reproducing the favorable local size/polarity/shape of the high-valued strained or reactive structures are not demonstrated. The observed labels do not reveal a unique missing pharmacophore.

Configurations are unspecified in the complex cages, and stable conventional heteroatom substitution is not reliably preserved. These are chemical coverage gaps, not proven score-improving requirements.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-2 cyclopropenyl imino/lactam structure scores 0.4758347412408679; its closely related methyl-substituted record scores 0.27042852516134586 and the hydroxyl-substituted final record 0.0032495986862503307. A related fused unsaturated small-ring substituent reaches 0.45842312287146847. These records associate constrained unsaturated carbon substitution with higher values within that series, but cannot separate size, composition and shape contributions. The highly caged seed-1 molecule scores 0.46181183363987727 despite its liabilities, and the acyclic seed-0 leader reaches 0.2999550904195335. An enlarged duplicated heterocycle scores 1.6298641881871607e-43, while late FCF scores 1.409300415191629e-22. Neither aromaticity, more rings nor smaller size alone explains the observed gradient.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-8916fdbd9300, complete frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 accepted records per session including 290 optimizer proposals; paired Parent n-a1818ac8ff05 uses the same panel. Across 4,350 Child optimizer records, molecule-level structure flags find 429 N-halogen, 135 O-halogen, 329 peroxide and 48 acyl-halide molecules, versus Parent counts 546, 241, 248 and 37. Some reactive groups occur in high-valued structures; label quality and chemical persistence therefore remain distinct. These are overlapping structural categories, not measured instability rates.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve ordinary heteroatom connectivity when adding halogens or oxygen.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to distinguish carbon halogenation, heteroatom halogenation, peroxide formation and acyl-halide formation as different chemical edits, and retain ordinary local alternatives for current-session comparison. Any benefit requires a new test; these associations do not attribute effects to the modified weighting component or justify a universal rejection gate.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-8916fdbd9300, complete frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 accepted records per session including 290 optimizer proposals; paired Parent n-a1818ac8ff05 uses the same panel. There are 4,180 ring-containing optimizer molecules and 456 with an unsaturated perceived ring of at most 4 atoms. One high-valued cage contains 9 perceived rings and 9 unassigned tetrahedral centres; another leader contains a cyclopropene substituent. The corresponding Parent small-ring flag count is 566, so this liability does not uniformly increase. Ring perception establishes connectivity, not feasible geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Rich ring construction is present, but reliable construction of feasible fused, bridged and unsaturated small rings is not demonstrated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent ring size, bridge topology, local unsaturation and geometric feasibility separately from merely having ring-closure digits. Preserve less strained alternatives with comparable polar/aromatic connections for task-local feedback; more rings, fewer small rings or a fixed scaffold class is not established as a universal improvement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-8916fdbd9300, complete frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 accepted records per session including 290 optimizer proposals; paired Parent n-a1818ac8ff05 uses the same panel. Child optimizer structures span 1 to 117 heavy atoms, with 126 at or below 6 and 355 at or above 50; the paired Parent has 85 and 150 in those descriptive bins. Both tiny fragments and repeated large assemblies occur at poor observed values, while some larger decorated structures retain useful values. This is a two-tail observation, not evidence for a common optimal size.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve a useful molecular scale during fragmentation and repeated core assembly.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Track destructive fragmentation and repeated scaffold growth against the chemically coherent structures already observed in the current session. Support core-preserving and core-rebuilding edits across sizes, and measure accepted outcomes without imposing a task-specific size target or promoting these descriptive bins into rewards or gates.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-8916fdbd9300, complete frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 accepted records per session including 290 optimizer proposals; paired Parent n-a1818ac8ff05 uses the same panel. Every digest has stereocentre_rate 0.0 and charged_rate 0.0; structure perception finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,517 of 4,350 Child proposals, versus 2,417 in the Parent. Several higher-valued families contain aliphatic amines. Neutral SMILES notation is not proof of nonionisability, and the trajectories do not identify preferred stereoisomers or protonation states.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted structures do not explicitly represent configurations or ionisation states even where molecular connectivity makes them relevant.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic representation would need explicit configuration and chemically reasonable ionisation handling, or at least ambiguity accounting, while retaining canonical identity and session isolation. Test its practical effect rather than assuming a configuration, charged form or extra stereoisomer is rewarded.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-8916fdbd9300, complete frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 accepted records per session including 290 optimizer proposals; paired Parent n-a1818ac8ff05 uses the same panel. The Child has 2,136 typed and 1,486 generic Murcko scaffold strings across optimizer molecules, compared with Parent 1,932 and 1,131; empty scaffolds are included. Yet several high-valued local series show exact label ties after halogen, phenol/thiol, carbonyl/thione or ketone/alcohol/acid edits. Much of the apparent variety includes unusual ring closures and repeated cores. Scaffold counts alone neither prove collapse nor demonstrate useful chemical breadth.
transferable_gaps.gap: Numerous graph variants do not establish useful exploration of chemically distinct, feasible core arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Distinguish core topology changes from peripheral substitutions and record which changes move current-session labels. Preserve feasible alternative cores while continuing feedback-based search. Treat scaffold diversity and fragment-excluded similarity as descriptive evidence, not objectives or component-attribution claims.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Fixed three full-archive experts: original count-dot Tanimoto, exact count-minmax Tanimoto and normalized-count Matern-3/2, using radius-2/2048/chirality count fingerprints.
Accepted-only current-session archive without feature deduplication; common full-archive empirical center/population SD floor 0.001, noise SD 0.05, unit amplitude and inherited jitter ladders.
Categorical selection of one exact correlated expert function per draw, original shared normal block and isolated categorical-uniform stream; sequential no-replacement maxima with first-index ties.
K=3/M=40 stall-conditioned mean eligibility and raw-score survivor/breeding/stall host. The Child encounters 116 stalled batches, but only 22 have certified allocation; 94 use fallback.
De novo graph generation, 64 greedy survivors, quantile parent draws, connected-fragment crossover/finishing and ordinary one/two/three mutation continuation.
Canonical parse/serialize-stable identity admission, source-relative sulfur-envelope gate, bounded valid generation-order fallback and fresh task-session state.
Failed-attempt crossover-probability reduction remains; the earlier removed rejection-conditioned mutation-call escalation is not reintroduced.
